description: Every kind of record ear writes on standard output (docs/design/node-framework.md section 8.8), one JSON object a line from one encoder (src/control/status_log.cpp), in the order the C++ test (src/control/tests/status_log_test.cpp) makes them. Each has v (the schema's version: additive changes keep it, a breaking one bumps it), seq (from 1; a gap is a record a full queue dropped, and the next record carries dropped and says so in msg: record 18 here is dropped), t (UTC, microseconds), kind, the kind's fields in this order, and msg, the plain line ear printed before records (jq -r .msg reads as ear always did). A graph-file record carries every diagnostic of its change; its msg is the lines it printed, joined by newlines (errors only). A log record names its node, or says unattributed; log records are paced per node, or per source when unattributed (32 at once, then one a second), and the next one that passes after a flood carries heldBack and says so in msg (the last log record here; records 20 to 51 passed but are not shown). Text from peers and libraries is escaped, never interpreted. A diagnostic record carries its structured fields (such as ms) between code and detail, and one that names no node (ear.data-loop-wedged) has no node field.
